title: Intra-oral scans show promise in detecting secondary caries
html:
Dental Tribune International

Fri. 20. November 2026

share save

PELOTAS, Brazil: Beyond their established applications, intra-oral scans could provide dentists with an additional tool for identifying caries around dental restorations. In what they believe is the first clinical validation study of its kind, researchers in Brazil have investigated whether conventional intra-oral scans—obtained without caries detection features—could identify secondary caries according to severity categories adapted from the Caries Associated with Restorations or Sealants criteria. Their findings suggest that the diagnostic value of these scans may depend on lesion severity.

Conducted at the Federal University of Pelotas, the study included 41 adult patients with a total of 299 amalgam or resin composite restorations. The researchers compared two diagnostic approaches: visual and tactile clinical examination and assessments of intra-oral scans, classifying each restoration as sound or showing initial, moderate or severe caries.

The clinical and intra-oral scan assessments frequently agreed, but the accuracy of the latter varied depending on the lesion severity. The examiner was generally successful at identifying initial lesions from the scans, had more difficulty detecting severe lesions and struggled particularly with moderate lesions. However, the examiner rarely classified sound restorations or those with initial lesions as having moderate or severe caries. The researchers attributed the difficulty in identifying moderate lesions partly to the challenge of assessing small enamel cavities and dentine shadows from scans alone.

The findings also reflect broader evidence on digital caries detection. A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis found that assessments based on images obtained by intra-oral scanners and cameras demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy and that their performance varied according to lesion location and examiner experience.

These findings suggest that intra-oral scans may be particularly useful for assessing visible changes around restorations, although their ability to detect lesions, particularly moderate ones, is limited. Overall, conventional intra-oral scans could offer useful additional information when monitoring restorations.

The study, titled “Validation of 3D intraoral scanner use for detecting caries lesions around dental restorations: A diagnostic accuracy study”, was published online on 19 October 2026 in Clinical Oral Investigations.
